strongest_confirmed_findings: Abilene's $15B JV over 1.2GW of facility power implies $12.5M per facility MW. Crusoe's 1.2-1.4 design PUE converts this to $15.0M-$17.5M per full-build IT MW.
At explicit 70%-90% utilization sensitivities, Abilene capital is $16.7M-$25.0M per effective utilized IT MW, $20.3M base. This is capital intensity, not revenue productivity.
Only Abilene's initial two 100MW buildings were confirmed operational as of June 9; OpenAI's more-than-10GW secured/committed milestone is not active or period-average MW.

NMED now marks Project Jupiter's microgrid air-permit process stayed by the New Mexico Supreme Court. FT separately reported approximately $18B of loans indicated at 89-91 cents; that market detail is secondary.
investable_read_through: OpenAI's $110B funding round and SoftBank's completed $64.6B cumulative investment are strong corporate-capital positives, but the infrastructure stack remains exposed to construction, permit, lease and refinancing timing. The current trade signal is dispersion: financed demand exists, yet project-level debt can weaken when delivery/permitting certainty deteriorates. Treat Oracle/STACK/Jupiter stress as an execution-risk indicator, not proof of OpenAI demand failure or project cancellation.
contradictions_to_prior_assumptions: The inherited $24.7B per IT-GW compute-content anchor lacked a verified project perimeter and is superseded as a canonical Stargate benchmark.
Secured or committed GW cannot be equated with active/billable MW. At Abilene, 200MW facility power was operational versus 1.2GW full-build design.
Abilene's 1.2-1.4 PUE is a design range, not measured operational performance; prior PUE=1 placeholders are invalid.
